clusters.headline_hint: Eritrea cuts diplomatic ties with Ethiopia amid renewed Tigray fighting and rising regional tensions

claims.text: Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on October 1, 2026, after accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts.
Eritrea's Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Thursday that it was severing all diplomatic ties with Ethiopia in response to the expulsion of its diplomats from Addis Ababa.
Ethiopia declared 10 Eritrean diplomats in Addis Ababa, including the charge d'affaires and diplomats accredited to the African Union, persona non grata and ordered them to leave within 48 hours.
Ethiopia's Ministry of Foreign Affairs accused Eritrea, Sudan, and Egypt of supporting an opposition alliance led by the Tigray People's Liberation Front.
Ethiopia annexed Eritrea in 1962, and Eritrea secured independence in 1993 following an armed struggle led by President Isaias Afwerki.
Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed moved to normalise diplomatic relations with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki when Abiy came to power in 2018.
The 2022 Pretoria Peace Agreement ended a two-year civil war between the Ethiopian federal government and the Tigray People's Liberation Front.

An opposition coalition against Ethiopia's federal government includes the Tigray People's Liberation Front, the Oromo Liberation Army, a faction of the Ogaden National Liberation Front, and militant groups from Benishangul-Gumuz and Afar.
A medic in the southern Tigrayan town of Alamata reported that 52 civilians died during three days of heavy fighting.
An African Union mediator estimated that 600,000 lives were lost during the civil war in Ethiopia between 2020 and 2022.
Eritrea's Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel denied that Eritrea was backing the newly formed rebel alliance fighting the Ethiopian government.
Ethiopia's National Intelligence and Security Service announced an indefinite ban on drone flights in Addis Ababa and surrounding areas.

clusters.headline_hint: High school student protests over poor conditions spread across France, prompting crisis meetings

claims.text: French police arrested 1,949 people and reported 305 police officers injured during nationwide high school protests on Thursday.
France's interior ministry reported that 1,027 out of 3,700 high schools across the country were affected by student actions, including blockades at 222 schools.
University students in France joined the high school demonstrations on Thursday, blocking access to about 30 university campuses.
Regional prefect authorities in Strasbourg ordered tram services to halt after protesting students placed barriers on the tracks.
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu held a crisis meeting on Thursday to address escalating student unrest across the country.
A bin fire at the Nelson Mandela high school in Nantes spread to the front of the building and damaged the entrance hall.
The headteacher at Degrugillier high school in Auchel sustained an ear injury from a firework during student protests.
French National Rally leader Marine Le Pen called for a new anti-rioting law, stating that the protests were "riots organized by professionals and overseen by deputies from La France Insoumise."
Protesters outside Saint-Exupery high school in Marseille forced firefighters to flee their vehicle before setting the fire truck on fire.
French Education Minister Édouard Geffray scheduled meetings for Friday with representative staff unions, parent groups, and student associations.
The French government announced that many high schools would switch to online classes due to safety concerns from ongoing student protests.
Interior Minister Laurent Nunez launched an internal police investigation following allegations of excessive force and brutality against three students.

clusters.headline_hint: US presses European allies to release emergency diesel stockpiles amid fuel price spikes and supply concerns

claims.text: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urged European partners on social media to immediately release strategic diesel reserves to address supply disruptions.
Average US diesel prices surged over 70 percent to $6.39 per gallon following the start of the US war on Iran, according to AAA data.
US President Donald Trump stated he was considering a potential ban on US diesel exports to curb domestic fuel costs.
French President Emmanuel Macron planned a video meeting of G7 leaders for mid-October to discuss coordinating releases of fuel reserves.
European Union trade chief Maros Sefcovic warned that any US ban on diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans" and cause "very dramatic consequences" for economic performance.
British ministers held calls on Thursday with counterparts from the European Commission, Germany, France, Italy, and Ireland to discuss drawing down emergency diesel reserves.
The average price of a litre of diesel in the United Kingdom reached a record high of 199.72p on Wednesday, according to the RAC.
Brent crude oil prices rose above $101 per barrel on Thursday, up from about $72 a barrel in February prior to the Iran war.
PetroChina cancelled October shipments of gasoline and jet fuel to destinations beyond Hong Kong and Macau to protect domestic supplies.
Russia extended its export ban on diesel for fuel producers through October 31 to maintain domestic fuel market stability.
Global trade intelligence firm Kpler reported that crude exports from the Gulf region reached 16.5 million barrels per day in September, returning to pre-war averages excluding Iran.
Kpler recorded that refined product shipments through the Strait of Hormuz averaged 677,000 barrels per day in late September, down from 3.6 million barrels per day before the Iran war.
Three Liberian-flagged oil tankers were struck by projectiles on Tuesday while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

clusters.headline_hint: Indian pilot praised after surviving cockpit stabbing on Flydubai flight as UAE probes terror link

claims.text: Flydubai Captain Smit Machchhar survived a knife attack by his co-pilot inside the cockpit on a flight carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv.
The cockpit attack forced the Flydubai flight to make an emergency landing in Tabuk in northwestern Saudi Arabia on Wednesday.
Captain Smit Machchhar was transferred to Abu Dhabi to recover from his injuries.
US President Donald Trump praised Captain Smit Machchhar as a hero for fighting off the knife attack and opening the cockpit door to call for help.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on X that Captain Smit Machchhar showed immense courage and that his quick actions prevented another 9/11-like attack.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu posted on X praising Captain Smit Machchhar for preventing a catastrophic midair disaster and saving 174 lives.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that the co-pilot behind the attack on the Flydubai flight had undergone Islamist radical indoctrination.
The UAE chief prosecutor announced an investigation into the Flydubai cockpit fight, including the possibility of terrorist activity or intent.
Saudi Arabia's interior ministry stated that the co-pilot was transferred to the United Arab Emirates on Thursday morning accompanied by an Emirati security team.
According to Flightradar24, the Flydubai flight plummeted around 17,000 feet in altitude in the span of a minute during the cockpit altercation.
Media reports indicated that 166 out of the 174 passengers aboard the Flydubai flight were Israeli citizens.
The co-pilot accused of attacking the captain is an Omani national.
US President Donald Trump stated that Tehran was likely involved in the Flydubai flight attack and warned that Iran would be hit very hard if it was responsible.
In an interview published by Time magazine, US President Donald Trump stated it was possible he might resume bombing Iran after the US midterm elections on November 3.
The Wall Street Journal reported that the United States was set to send a third aircraft carrier and up to 10,000 extra service members to the Middle East by late November.
Saudi Arabia's Interior Ministry stated that Flydubai flight FZ1073 landed safely in Tabuk at 9:45 am local time with 174 passengers and eight crew members on board.
All 174 passengers from the diverted Flydubai flight continued their journey to Tel Aviv at approximately 5:40 pm on Wednesday on a replacement aircraft.
UAE Attorney General Hamad Saif Al Shamsi launched an official investigation into whether the cockpit attack involved terrorist intent or prior planning.
Authorities from Saudi Arabia, Israel, the UAE, the United States, and Oman are jointly involved in efforts to determine the motive behind the Flydubai attack.
Israeli intelligence and security officials traveled to Saudi Arabia to assist with the investigation into the Flydubai flight incident.

clusters.headline_hint: ECI orders probe into alleged fraudulent Form 7 voter deletion applications in Karnataka

claims.text: Cockroach Janta Party leader Abhijeet Dipke demanded the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and announced a protest in Mumbai for October 2.
The Cockroach Janta Party demanded putting the Special Intensive Revision on hold, reinstating the January 2025 voter list, and scrapping 2023 Election Commission legislation.
The Election Commission of India dismissed claims of an internal breakdown, stating all three commissioners were in agreement on decisions regarding the Special Intensive Revision.
Mumbai Police denied permission for the Cockroach Janta Party's October 2 protest at Shivaji Park, citing a 2013 Bombay High Court order.
The Election Commission of India ordered a probe into bulk Form-7 voter deletion filings following a five-hour protest by Karnataka Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar.

Chief Electoral Officer of Karnataka V. Anbu Kumar directed Electoral Registration Officers to act against applicants submitting false Form-7 voter deletion claims under Section 31 of the Representation of the People Act, 1950.
Karnataka Police registered five FIRs on October 1, 2026, over bulk Form-7 filings under the Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, 2023.
Leader of the Opposition Rahul Gandhi stated that BJP and Election Commission officials colluded to fill out Form-7s in bulk to delete targeted voters.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke claimed that approximately 13 crore voters have been deleted from Indian electoral rolls since 2024.
Leaders from 21 Opposition parties met in New Delhi on September 30 to outline a joint strategy against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
According to a report by The Hindu, a majority of the 4,000 Form 7 voter deletion applications filed during Karnataka's Special Intensive Revision targeted Muslim voters.
In Vijayapura district's Babaleshwar constituency, 1,363 out of 1,373 Form 7 applications filed on September 22 were submitted by just 10 individuals.
In Bhalki in Bidar district, 30 individuals submitted over 1,700 Form 7 voter deletion applications on September 23.
The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi formally objected 14 times in 10 months to decisions regarding the Special Intensive Revision.
Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke called Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar a puppet of Amit Shah and Narendra Modi during a press conference in Mumbai on October 1, 2026.
The Cockroach Janta Party demanded that future Indian elections be conducted using paper ballots rather than Electronic Voting Machines.
